chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurari, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Salih ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: I heard him saying:
"Dive deep into your hearts, and if Allah has purified them from the stirring of misgivings and displeasure at anything of His making, then when you find them so, ask Him for whatever you wish."

key_terms.الواجس: Inner whisperings, misgivings, anxious thoughts that stir within the soul
key_terms.تبحروا: Dive deep, probe thoroughly -- from bahr (sea), meaning to plunge into the depths
key_terms.سخط: Displeasure, anger, resentment -- specifically at God's decree
key_terms.صنعه: His making, His creation -- refers to God's actions and decrees

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about purifying the heart before supplication?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) instructs believers to examine their hearts deeply, seeking whether God has cleansed them from inner doubts and resentment toward His decree. This teaching, delivered to his close circle of students, emphasizes that the prerequisite for effective supplication is a heart free of objection to divine will -- a concept central to the Shia spiritual tradition of tawakkul (reliance on God).
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
